subject: living/dodo
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: plant or animal atlas card.
ONE landscape 3:2 natural-history field-sketchbook page. Visible loose graphite construction lines, fine sepia ink hatching and restrained uneven watercolour washes, with realistic species colours kept softly muted. Detailed main subject, irregular unfinished edges dissolving into warm cream lightly foxed paper. An observed working sketch, not a photograph, glossy painting, digital render or infographic. No writing, labels, numbers, signature, watermark, border or binding. Prioritise diagnostic anatomy and botanical structure; no invented hybrid species. No obligatory explorer, human hands or portrait. A single main composition, with a separate small specimen only when specifically requested.
Subject: Reconstructed Raphus cucullatus in Mauritian coastal forest, full side view, sturdy but not obese grey-brown body, tiny real wings, tuft of pale curled tail feathers, strong yellow-grey legs, large hooked two-tone bill. Natural alert bird on fallen leaves, not comic fat caricature or turkey, no humans.
Study the plant or animal itself. Maintain believable scale, structural continuity, natural pose and habitat. Do not turn this into a generic explorer scene. Treat extinct animals as restrained evidence-informed reconstructions.
